# 03 Wipe

Full definition: [TAXONOMY.md](../../TAXONOMY.md), section 3.

**What belongs here.** A moving, designed boundary separates A from B until B fills the frame.

**Test.** Is there an edge with A on one side and B on the other, travelling until B fills the frame?

**Not here.** A third layer covering the frame makes it 04 Cover. Slices of A moving away make it 05 Motion › Split. A mask taken from footage brightness makes it 02 Blend › Luma Dissolve.

**Build.** Remotion built-ins: wipe(), clockWipe(), iris(). Otherwise, a direct mask presentation.

## Subfamilies

| Folder | What goes in it | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| [Linear](linear/) | A straight edge sweeps across. | left-to-right, diagonal, soft gradient wipe |
| [Iris](iris/) | A circle or shape grows from, or shrinks to, a point. | iris in/out, keyhole |
| [Clock](clock/) | An edge rotates around a centre. | clock wipe, radar sweep |
| [Shape Mask](shape-mask/) | B appears through a growing designed shape. | logo reveal, letterform mask |
| [Pattern](pattern/) | Many small edges at once, in a grid or repeat. | blinds, checkerboard, halftone, stripes |
| [Organic](organic/) | An irregular, noise-driven edge, with no full cover. | ink-edge wipe, liquid edge straight to B |

## Transitions in this family

| Transition | Subfamily | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [Linear Wipe](linear/linear-wipe/) | Linear | A straight edge sweeps across the frame at any angle, hard or soft. Split mode opens from the middle like barn doors. |
| [Iris](iris/iris/) | Iris | A circle opens from a point and grows until the new scene fills the frame. |
| [Rounded Reveal](shape-mask/rounded-reveal/) | Shape Mask | The new scene opens in a rounded window that grows from the centre to full frame, settling from a slight zoom inside. |
| [Text Mask Zoom](shape-mask/text-mask/) | Shape Mask | A word appears with the new scene inside its letters, then zooms through one letter until the new scene fills the frame. |
| [Halftone Wipe](pattern/halftone-wipe/) | Pattern | A wave of dots grows across the frame, from tiny to touching, with the new scene inside them. |
| [Stripe Wipe](pattern/stripe-wipe/) | Pattern | Diagonal stripes of the new scene open one after another and widen until they join. |
| [Noise Wipe](organic/noise-wipe/) | Organic | A ragged, noise-driven edge sweeps across the frame, like a torn or eroded border. |
